### Observed differences

- Two activities that never appeared earlier now run in every case: A01 and A05 each went from 0 of 200 cases to about 200 of 200, occurring exactly once per case (no repeats in either window). [OCC001, OCC002]
- In the later window, A01 sits around the middle of the case (median position about 0.6 of the trace) and its transitions lead mostly to A06 (about 80 in 100), with small shares to A02, A03 and A04. [POS001, DIR001]
- A05 sits at the end (median position 1.0); only about 29 of 200 cases show a transition out of A05, and of those roughly 59 in 100 lead to A04 and 31 in 100 to A02. [POS003, DIR004]
- Earlier, A01 co-occurred with no other traced activity, and A06 always appeared without A05; in the later window A01 co-occurs with A03, A04, A06 and A05 in essentially every case — usually after A03 (about 87 in 100) and after A04 (about 69 in 100), and always before A06 and before A05. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004]
- A05 now co-occurs with the existing activities in a fixed late slot: after A06 in all cases, after A03 in about 98 in 100 and after A04 in about 87 in 100 cases. [REL005, REL006, REL007]
- Routing around A06 changed: earlier, A06's outgoing transitions went to A02 (about 53 in 100), A04 (29) and A03 (19); in the later window about 84 in 100 lead to A05, with only small shares to A02, A04 and A03. A03 and A04 now also lead to A01 (about 45 and 52 in 100 of their transitions), which was not a target before, while A04's transitions to A06 fell from about 74 in 100 to about 6 in 100. [DIR005, DIR002, DIR003]
- Step distances grew where a new activity now sits between existing ones: A04-to-A06 gaps moved from mostly 1 step (about 74 in 100) to 2–3 steps (about 93 in 100), A03-to-A06 gaps from 1–3 steps to 2–4 steps, and A03-to-A04 gaps of 4–5 steps appeared (about 28 in 100). [LAG003, LAG002, LAG001]
- Existing activities shifted slightly earlier in the case: A04's median position fell from about 0.67 to 0.4, and A06's mean position from about 0.83 to 0.72. [POS002, POS004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the process executes two activities that it did not execute before: A01 once per case in the middle — typically after A03 or A04 and before A06 — and A05 once per case at the end, after A06. Earlier, cases ran from A03/A04 onward to A06 (or directly to A02) without these two activities; in the later window the dominant chain is A03/A04 → A01 → A06 → A05. [OCC001, OCC002, REL003, REL004, REL007, DIR001, DIR005]

Supporting signs: participation went from zero to all 200 cases for both activities; each holds fixed-order relations with all major existing activities; A01 and A05 gained outgoing transitions, and A06 — which earlier often ended the case — now leads to A05 in about 84 in 100 of its transitions; and the step distance between A03/A04 and A06 grew by roughly one step, consistent with A01 sitting between them. The screening produced 21 qualifying items where about 0.13 would be expected if nothing had changed, so sampling variation cannot account for the pattern as a whole. [OCC001, OCC002, REL001, REL002, REL005, REL006, DIR003, DIR005, LAG002, LAG003]

Limitations: the items are not independent — most reflect the same two additions rather than separate differences — and the evidence cannot rule out that A01 and A05 were simply not recorded in the earlier window rather than absent from execution. A05's outgoing profile rests on only about 29 cases, so its successors remain uncertain, and A01's placement varies (A04 precedes A01 in only about 69 in 100 cases), so its insertion point is not entirely fixed. [DIR004, REL002]

Other differences: the earlier positions of A04 and A06 and the longer A03–A04 gaps noted above are consistent with consequences of the same additions rather than separate behavioural changes. [POS002, POS004, LAG001]
